recipes.name: Patriotic Fruit Pizza
ingredients_raw: 3 large bananas, sliced - or as needed
1 tablespoon lemon juice, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt in a bowl; set aside.

Mash vegetable shortening and margarine together in a large bowl until thoroughly combined; beat in 1 ½ cups sugar, eggs, and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract. Stir in flour mixture until forms a workable dough; spread into a rectangle shape on an ungreased 12x17-inch baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until very lightly browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Cool completely.

Meanwhile, mash cream cheese with remaining each 1 cup sugar and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract in a bowl until smooth. Place sliced bananas in a separate bowl; gently toss with lemon juice to prevent browning.

Spread cream cheese mixture over cookie base in an even layer to cover; smooth. Place blueberries in neat, closely spaced rows in a square in the upper left corner for the stars. Arrange alternating rows of sliced bananas and sliced strawberries across pizza for the stripes. Refrigerate leftovers.

raw_recipe.headline: Patriotic Fruit Pizza
raw_recipe.description: This patriotic fruit pizza recipe features a sweet cookie crust topped with bananas, strawberries, and blueberries decorated like stars and stripes.

video.description: Show your patriotic colors with a sweet summer fruit pizza that combines clever colors and fresh fruit with refreshing and bright flavors. Begin by making a sugar cookie crust with flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, salt, vegetable shortening, margarine, sugar, eggs and vanilla. Then spread on a filling of cream cheese, sugar and vanilla. Toss banana slices in lemon juice and place on pizza in alternating stripes with strawberries, paving out a rectangle in the corner for blueberries. Bring one to the 4th of July potluck to celebrate Independence with great taste!

review.reviewBody:
BEST DESSERT EVER!! Huge family hit! A new favorite for the holidays!!!
Here's a tip: We only had 1 package of cream cheese, so we used 1/2 a can of Reddi Whip instead and it was awesome!! Made it very creamy but not too thick!!

I have made this twice in the past week and it was a big hit both times. The second time, I cut the recipe in half and baked in a 12' round pizza pan. I didn't use bananas, just strawberries and blueberries in a random pattern.

This was a huge hit after our church's patriotic music program! I added the grated peel of one lemon to the cookie dough, and used 1 C. butter in place of the shortening and margarine, as another reviewer suggested. I didn't arrange the blueberries in rows, just outlined the rectangle and filled it in however they fell. Beautiful to look at and scrumptious to eat! I plan on making it again for another 4th of July event.
This was very tasty. I did make a graham cracker crust instead of the sugar cookie crust. Very tasty and will make it again

I was so glad to find this recipe; it was perfect for our 4th of July picnic! I got some really great local fresh grown strawberries, blue berries, and I also used some fresh raspberries at a local farmers stand along one of our back roads in Lancaster, PA. I liked that this was a completely made from scratch recipe, instead of using ‘boxed’ sugar cookies. My only change was that I used 1 cup of unsalted butter instead of ½ cup shortening and ½ cup butter. It turned out perfect, and it looks so impressive, but was really quite easy!

This was a big hit with my family and coworkers. I followed the suggestions of other reviewers and used all butter. I also reduced the sugar In the cream cheese topping to 3/4C and drizzled apricot preserves over the top.

This got RAVE REVIEWS with my family at our Independence Day dinner last night. The ONLY thing that I would change for the future is adding only 3/4 cup sugar to the cream cheese spread, it was a little too sweet for my taste. I'd give 4.5 stars if possible.

I made this last 4th of July and my recruiter family divoured it in 2 days!!! I used raspberries instead of strawberries because of an allergy, but it was still amazing! Can't wait to make it again this year!!!!!!!!!
This was a delicious recipe and easy to make. I made it for the Fourth of July and it was a hit with the grandkids and adults alike.
I love this recipe and have made it several times. I make my icing a little less sweet based on personal preference.
Everyone in my family, as well as my neighbor, loved it! I might try raspberries instead of strawberries next time.

MY family LOVED this cookie cake. My son birthday is on the 4th of July, and my kids love cookie cakes. What a prefect match and they loved the cookie cake so much that I made it again for the weekend party with relatives. And they loved it, I added some mini chocolate chips to the mix and that was a delicious addition. It's a keeper, it's also super easy to make. Thanks
Next time I will add sugar to the mix or frosting or pudding. I like a sweeter dessert.
I couldn't find any blueberries, but instead I put black grapes and it till tasted good. I'll definitely make this again next year.

This pizza was big hit @ the family picnic! I must admit, I was in a hurry so cheated & used store purchased frig cookie dough or the crust but, after reading thru the reviews, I'll definitely try the "scratch' version next time. I also believe that the cream cheese could be cut in half as it seems to over-power the wonderful flavors of the fruit. 
Experimentation! That's how we learn & discover!! 
Enjoy your version! ~
